subject: Digital Electronics
course: Edge AI and Embedded Machine Learning
learning_objective: Compare one shared weight scale with a separate scale for each output channel, making loss in a small-range channel visible.
core_conclusion: Per-channel scales match different channel ranges and preserve small weights that a large shared scale coarsens.

terminology.scope: Official terminology basis from saved course research; all numerical examples are explicitly illustrative.

scenes.heading: Channels have different ranges
lines: Two output channels, two scales of magnitude.
scenes.change: Two weight rows extend to their own maxima; channel A receives a zoom inset while a common-scale overview retains its much smaller magnitude.
scenes.cause: Different filters can contain very different weight ranges.
scenes.result: Both actual maxima and the zoom factor are explicit.
scenes.timing_reason: 3 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 2 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: One scale follows the largest weight
scenes.change: All weights quantize using the largest magnitude2; A’s0.01 and0.02 both land at code1 while0.04 lands at3.
scenes.cause: A tensor-wide scale is set by the largest channel range.
scenes.result: Distinct small weights collapse onto the same code and reconstruction.
scenes.timing_reason: 5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Give each channel its own ruler
scenes.change: Channel A’s ruler contracts to its own range, spreading codes to32,64,127; B retains its previous ruler.
scenes.cause: Per-output-channel symmetric scales normalize each channel independently.
scenes.result: A’s three weights occupy distinct codes and reconstruct near their originals.
scenes.timing_reason: 6.5 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3.5 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

scenes.heading: Compare the same small channel
lines: Lower error is visible in the residuals.
scenes.change: The shared and per-channel reconstructions align on identical axes; residual bars extend by absolute reconstruction errors, with per-channel residuals visibly smaller.
scenes.cause: Only the scale choice changed, so the residual difference isolates its effect.
scenes.result: A mean-absolute-error pair is computed from the displayed reconstructions.
scenes.timing_reason: 4 seconds for the stated object transformation, then 3 seconds to inspect its numerical result.

critical_processes.uncertainty: A zoomed axis might falsely claim better accuracy; labels might imply every channel always benefits.
critical_processes.expected_observation: Original A values remain unchanged on shared comparison axes; per-channel codes separate the two previously collapsed small weights.

risk_moments.reason: Two distinct A values must actually map to one shared code.
B scale stays fixed while A scale changes.
Before/after residuals must use the same real-value gain.

bindings: channelScales(channels) → per-channel scale labels and quantize calls
quantized channel entries → code values and reconstruction markers
absolute errors → residual widths and mean error cells

title: Per-Channel Weight Quantization: Preserving Small Weights
prompt:
Create a 30-second silent English animation of Per-Channel Weight Quantization. At 0–5 s, compare channel A weights 0.01, 0.02 and 0.04 against channel B weights 0.5, 1 and 2. At 5–13 s, quantize with shared scale 2/127 so A codes become 1, 1 and 3. At 13–23 s, use A scale 0.04/127 and keep B scale unchanged; A codes separate into 32, 64 and 127. At 23–30 s, compare absolute reconstruction errors on the same real-value scale and show the smaller per-channel error.

Render a 1920×1080, 16:9 MP4 at 30 fps with no audio, using Helvetica Neue and line height 1.45. Use background layers #0e0e0e, #171b1c and #212629; input #56b4e9, operations #e69f00, results #009e73, clipping or rejection #d55e00, and secondary weights #cc79a7, with strong text #f8fafc and muted text #a8b4c4. Keep concise copy left and a large numerical SVG diagram right; fade and slide labels over 12–18 frames with 10-frame staggering, and bind moving marks, values and arithmetic to the same mechanism state.
